loss_definition: mean per-pixel cross-entropy, raw softmax, out-of-fold model, 512x640

inspection.method: each of the 20 frames viewed as photograph | ground truth overlay | model prediction overlay (local images, not published); judged by one reviewer (the assistant), not a domain expert; the judgement is a visual impression, not a validated annotation audit
inspection.what_was_seen: In every frame the ground truth is a plausible, smooth and frame-to-frame consistent labelling (the whole visible kidney surface as kidney-parenchyma, covered kidney and intestine at the edges, instruments outlined correctly). The model's mask for the same frames hedges between kidney-parenchyma, covered-kidney and untinted background tissue in large patches, while the instruments are segmented well. 14 of the 20 are from train/seq_16 and 6 from train/seq_5.

upper_bound.statement: 0 of 20 inspected top-loss frames look like label error. An exact one-sided 95% upper bound on the share of label errors among frames like these is 13.9% (1 - 0.05^(1/20)).

answer: The out-of-fold loss ranking surfaces model failures on tissue classes, not label errors. Only 1 of the top 20 is a gate failure at all (official IoU below 0.5), out of 310 such frames among the 2235 training frames (13.9%). So label error of the kind this probe can find accounts for none of the gate failures seen and, among top-loss frames, for at most about 14%. The probe does not look at instrument-label errors specifically and cannot rule out a few wrong instrument labels outside the top 20.
